papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for 6G Communication Networks: State-of-the-Art and Vision for the Future
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sec. I (introduction and contributions), Sec. V.C (challenges), Sec. VI (conclusions); Secs. II-IV not read in detail.
papers.what_it_is: A review and vision paper on machine learning, quantum computing and quantum machine learning for 6G and beyond-5G wireless networks, proposing a QC-assisted ML and QML-based framework.

assertions.value: The authors state that, to their best knowledge, their work is the first to explicitly investigate the deployment of the QML framework for future communication networks.
quotes: To the authors' best knowledge, this work is the first to explicitly investigate the deployment of the QML framework for future communication networks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors priority claim; not independently checked.

assertions.value: The authors state that to date there is no investigation of the joint deployment of QC and ML for future communications, either using QC-assisted ML or the QML framework.
quotes: However, to-date there is no investigation of the joint deployment of QC and ML for future communications, either using QC-assisted ML or the QML framework.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors statement about the literature as of early 2019; the search scope is not described in the passages read.

assertions.value: The paper states that Google has announced a 72 qubit superconducting quantum computer.
quotes: Recently, Google has announced a 72 qubit superconducting quantum computer
assertions.certainty_reason: A 2019 survey passing on an announcement; the paper measures nothing here.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum machine learning for image classification
papers.version_note: File is arXiv:2304.09224v2 (28 Mar 2024), which notes that the published version is Mach. Learn.: Sci. Technol. 5:015040 (2024).
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, results text on MNIST, Medical MNIST and CIFAR-10, quanvolutional results, and Conclusion; appendix details not read.
papers.what_it_is: A model-proposal paper introducing two hybrid quantum-classical neural networks (parallel quantum circuits; quanvolutional layer) and comparing each to a classical counterpart on image datasets.

assertions.value: On the MNIST test data, the HQNN-Parallel model reached 99.21% accuracy and the CNN reached 98.71%; the classical model has 8 times more variational parameters than the hybrid one.
quotes: The HQNN has a 99.21% accuracy on the test data and outperforms the CNN which has a 98.71% accuracy. The classical model has 8 times more variational parameters than the hybrid one.
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured result on one dataset and one architecture pair; the passages read do not say whether the quantum layers ran on hardware.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against a single classical counterpart; no spread over seeds is given for these figures in the passages read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quanvolutional layer uses four times fewer weights than the classical analog and reaches approximately the same classification accuracy.
quotes: The quanvolutional layer uses fewer weights, four times less than the classical analog, to achieve approximately the same classification accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured over ten models per the Conclusion; the dataset is named in the body, which I did not quote.
assertions.reader_inference: I did not confirm the dataset behind the 67% figure in the passages read.

assertions.value: The authors state that a reduced number of weights does not imply increased efficiency of the hybrid approach, because the hybrid model trains more slowly than a classical model with the same number of weights.
quotes: However, the reduced number of weights does not imply increased efficiency of the hybrid approach due to the slower training of the hybrid model compared to the classical one with the same number of weights.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors statement of a limitation, from their own training runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that they recognize the need for broader validation across diverse datasets and real-world scenarios.
quotes: However, we recognize the need for broader validation to ensure holistic generalization across diverse datasets and real-world scenarios.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors own stated limitation.

papers.title_in_file: A Survey of Quantum Learning Theory
papers.version_note: The printed title omits the Guest Column prefix given in the record title.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sec. 1 Introduction, Sec. 6 Conclusion; Secs. 2-5 (proofs and algorithms) not read.
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum learning theory covering exact learning from membership queries, and PAC and agnostic learning from classical or quantum examples.

assertions.value: The survey states that the number of quantum membership queries needed to exactly learn a target concept can be polynomially smaller than the classical number, but not much smaller.
quotes: The number of quantum membership queries needed to exactly learn a target concept can be polynomially smaller than the number of classical membership queries, but not much smaller than that.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey summarizing proved theorems from the literature.

assertions.value: For the distribution-independent models of PAC and agnostic learning, the survey states that quantum examples give no significant advantage over classical random examples, while for some fixed distributions such as the uniform one quantum examples can be much better.
quotes: For the distribution-independent models of PAC and agnostic learning, quantum examples give no significant advantage over classical random examples
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey summarizing proved results of the authors and others.

assertions.value: The survey states that there exist concept classes that can be learned superpolynomially faster by quantum computers than by classical computers, for instance based on the Shor or Simon algorithm.
quotes: There exist concept classes that can be learned superpolynomially faster by quantum computers than by classical computers
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey summary of separations; Sec. 1 says they hold under reasonable complexity-theoretic assumptions.

assertions.value: Among its open questions the survey asks whether practical machine learning problems with a large provable quantum speed-up can be found.
quotes: Can we find practical machine learning problems with a large provable quantum speed-up?
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated by the authors as an open question as of 2017.

papers.title_in_file: Does provable absence of barren plateaus imply classical simulability?
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sec. I Introduction, Sec. VI Conclusions; Secs. II-V case-by-case analysis not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: A perspective article collecting case-by-case evidence that many models with provably barren-plateau-free loss landscapes admit classical simulation, with stated caveats.

assertions.value: The authors collect evidence, on a case-by-case basis, that many commonly used models whose loss landscapes avoid barren plateaus can also admit classical simulation, provided some classical data are collected from quantum devices during an initial data acquisition phase.
quotes: We collect evidence--on a case-by-case basis--that many commonly used models whose loss landscapes avoid barren plateaus can also admit classical simulation
assertions.certainty_reason: Perspective with case-by-case arguments, not a general proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that although for all their case studies the ingredients for simulation can be identified, they do not prove this will always be possible.
quotes: while for all our case studies it is possible to identify the ingredients necessary for simulation, we do not prove that this will always be possible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors explicit limitation of their own argument.

assertions.value: The authors state that their argument does not cover all possible quantum learning protocols.
quotes: However, it does not cover all possible quantum learning protocols.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors stated scope condition; the preceding sentence limits the argument to losses formulated as expectation values of an observable.

assertions.value: The authors state that their conclusions push against current practice in the community and that variational quantum algorithms need a rethink.
quotes: our conclusions push against current practice in the community and the net result is that variational quantum algorithms need a rethink.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors opinion in the conclusions.

papers.what_it_is: A short note (arXiv quant-ph/0107012) suggesting a quantum neural network built from optical modes, beam splitters and phase shifters, with a perceptron-like learning rule.

assertions.value: For a quantum perceptron with the identity operator as F, the author states that for small step size and normalized input states the iteration of the proposed learning rule converges to the desired state.
quotes: the result of iteration converges to the desired state
assertions.certainty_reason: Short analytic argument for a simplistic case; the note contains no simulation or experiment.

assertions.value: The author states that the proposed learning rule does not observe unitarity in general, so that light attenuation may take place besides phase rotations, and leaves this for future consideration.
quotes: The learning rule (6) may cause questions, for it does not observe the unitarity in general
assertions.certainty_reason: Author own stated limitation.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Methods for Neural Networks and Application to Medical Image Classification
papers.version_note: File is arXiv:2212.07389v1 (14 Dec 2022); a published version may differ.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sec. 1 introduction, experiments discussion and conclusion text (Fig. 13-16, Table 2 discussion); proofs and circuit details not read.
papers.what_it_is: A methods paper proposing quantum-assisted neural networks and quantum orthogonal neural networks (pyramidal circuit), with simulations and IBM hardware experiments on medical image classification.

assertions.value: The authors state that, from simulation and hardware experiments, quantum neural networks can be trained to the same level of accuracy as their classical counterparts for a number of classification tasks, while for more difficult tasks accuracy levels start to drop due to quantum hardware limitations.
quotes: we see that for a number of classification tasks the quantum neural networks can be indeed trained to the same level of accuracy as their classical counterparts
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured on small MedMNIST subsets, with images reduced by PCA to 4 or 8 dimensions, on simulators and IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that current hardware is not ready to perform medical image classification in a way that is competitive with classical neural networks, since the hardware does not have sufficient number and quality of qubits.
quotes: since the hardware does not have sufficient number and quality of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors own assessment from their hardware runs.

assertions.value: When both training and forward inference ran on the quantum computer, the authors report that the [4, 4, 2] network trained with a small drop in accuracy and the [8, 4, 2] network did not train at all, predicting always the same classification value.
quotes: the [8, 4, 2] neural network did not train at all, predicting always the same classification value for the entire dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured hardware result for two small architectures; the authors attribute the drop mainly to noise accumulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that their way of training optimizes the parameters of the pyramidal circuit gates, which allows training in time O(n2) instead of the previously known O(n3).
quotes: which allows for a training in time O(n2) instead of the previously known O(n3)
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors complexity claim; exponents are flattened by text extraction.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Neural Network for Quantum Neural Computing
papers.version_note: File is arXiv:2305.08544v1 (16 May 2023); a published version may differ.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Simulations section, Discussion with limitations; Methods and model derivation not read in detail.
papers.what_it_is: A model-proposal paper introducing soft quantum neurons built from classically-controlled single-qubit operations and measurements, benchmarked in numerical simulation on XOR, nonlinear datasets and handwritten digits.

assertions.value: In the simulated circles-dataset task, a soft quantum perceptron can achieve up to 96% accuracy when the probability of a bit flip is as high as 0.49.
quotes: In particular, a soft quantum perceptron can achieve up to 96% accuracy when the probability of a bit flip is as high as 0.49.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation of a small two-dimensional task with a modeled noise channel; not hardware.

assertions.value: On the moons dataset the classical MLP achieved 100% accuracy, slightly higher than the 99% accuracy of the soft quantum perceptron.
quotes: The MLP achieved 100% accuracy, which is slightly higher than the 99% accuracy of the soft quantum perceptron.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation on one small synthetic dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that there may also be a barren plateau in the loss function landscape of their model, which hinders further optimization of the network.
quotes: there may also be a barren plateau in the loss function landscape
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors own stated limitation.

papers.title_in_file: On Quantum Methods for Machine Learning Problems Part I: Quantum Tools
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Sec. 1 introduction, Sec. 4.2 Grover discussion text, Sec. 5 Conclusion; derivations and algorithm listings not read (text extraction garbles the math).
papers.what_it_is: A review (part I of two) presenting quantum computing basics and quantum tools such as Grover search and SWAP-test for use in classification and clustering.

assertions.value: The authors describe part one as presenting the fundamentals of qubits, quantum registers and quantum states, and introducing quantum tools based on known quantum search algorithms and SWAP-test.
quotes: introduces important quantum tools based on known quantum search algorithms and SWAP-test
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors description of the review contents.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum maximum/minimum search algorithms based on Grover search play essential roles as subroutines in different quantum algorithms for classification problems.
quotes: These quantum algorithms play essential roles as subroutines in different quantum algorithms for classification problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors framing statement in a review.
